## Summary

Research confidence is **Low**. Most of this break's ideal conditions are not yet confirmed by sources. It is the class the app computes from the evidence (how well the break's ideal conditions are documented), not a forecast and not a probability.

Main gaps:

- The sources found do not support this break's listed size range.
- Sources disagree about the best tide.
- Limited information is available about the shape of the bottom at this break.
- Limited information is available about the swell period this break needs.

Research notes (research_evidence.json):

> 9 sources, all read directly. 8 publishers (WSL counted once). TIDE CONFLICT, which the profile should resolve. Surf-Forecast says best around low tide. WannaSurf says low and mid. Surf Girl NZ, Surfara and MyWaveFinder say all tides, adding that low tide is hollower and faster and high tide mellower or chunkier. Only Strike Mission's model profile says mid. Several sources agree the wave is more hollow at low tide. Consider changing the profile from 'mid' to 'low_to_mid' or 'all'. SWELL DIRECTION: Surf-Forecast, Surf Girl NZ, Surfara and MyWaveFinder all say SW (225), inside the 220-260 optimum; Strike Mission's profile is WSW 210-280. WannaSurf's NW/W is the outlier (it may describe the swell window rather than the best direction). WIND: SE (135) from Surf-Forecast (offshore), Surf Girl NZ and Surfara; WannaSurf SW/S/SE. All agree with 140. MyWaveFinder says E and Strike Mission's profile says E (90, offshore range 50-130); both are 50 deg off and marked as contradicting. Surf-Forecast notes waves can be OK in light onshore winds. Size: Wikipedia 2-10 ft+, WannaSurf 3-16 ft+, WSL best contest day 4-5 ft. These overlap the profile's 3-12. Period: no source gives a number apart from Strike Mission's 14 s reference (model input). Surf-Forecast and Surfara say mostly groundswell. The 11/15 s profile values are otherwise unsupported. Season: WSL scheduled the 2026 CT for May 15-25, 'the optimal time of year'. MyWaveFinder says Mar-Jun (Raglan generally) and Strike Mission Mar-Oct. All are inside the profile's Mar-Oct. Strike Mission matches the profile's season and swell window almost exactly, which is a circularity warning: treat it as another app's assumptions. Independence: Surf Girl NZ and MyWaveFinder share near-identical text, and Surfara and MyWaveFinder share the sentence 'rocky point break is consistently fed by south westerly ground swells throughout the year'. These three community sources are probably one origin. Bathymetry: WannaSurf says a boulder bottom with a hard reef 'ledge' section toward Whale Bay; no survey or readable peer-reviewed bathymetry. The Scarfe et al. 2009 JCR abstract and the 1996 Waikato District Council reserve plan (scanned PDF) could not be read.

## Conflicting information

- **Swell direction · ideal bearing**: Surf-Forecast, Surf Girl NZ, Surfara and MyWaveFinder give southwest (the last three probably share one origin), Strike Mission's scoring profile favours WSW 210-280 deg (model inputs), whereas WannaSurf lists northwest and west as good swell directions.
- **Wind · offshore**: Surf-Forecast says offshore winds are from the southeast and Surf Girl NZ and Surfara give SE as optimal, WannaSurf lists SW, S and SE, whereas MyWaveFinder gives east and Strike Mission's model profile prefers east with an offshore range of 50-130 deg.
- **Tide · preferred stage**: Surf-Forecast says best around low tide, WannaSurf low and mid, Surf Girl NZ, Surfara and MyWaveFinder all tides, and Strike Mission's model profile mid; WannaSurf, Surfara, Surf Girl NZ and MyWaveFinder agree the wave is hollower at low tide and mellower or chunkier at high tide.
